title: Extensions and maintenance
goal: Design an original teaching extension and verify compatibility and disabling.
prerequisites: onec.p11; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Design an original teaching extension and verify compatibility and disabling.
Specify base version and extension points.
sections: An extension develops a solution within defined boundaries without uncontrolled base edits. State borrowed objects and modified methods. Use an original course configuration, not a proprietary standard solution. Avoiding direct base edits does not eliminate risks to data or behavior.

Start final engineering work from an independent, bounded assignment. Define domain, model, keys, rules and observable workflows. Declare templates and own changes. Reviewers should reproduce from the package without private data. File count, code volume and attractive screens do not replace correctness, preservation and clear reasoning about accepted choices and rejected alternatives.

Bind the extension to exact base version, compatibility mode and source hash. Changes to borrowed methods can invalidate assumptions after an upgrade. Do not claim all-future compatibility. List accepted, rejected and untested combinations; similar build numbers do not transferPASS.

Version binds source, tools, configuration format and infobase. Extensions additionally bind base configuration/dependencies. Build in fresh directories without cleaning prior work. Conflict resolution must not casually replace object identity. Preserve competing versions/requirements and prove the merged interpretation through tests. Repository operations alone are not native runtime evidence or a license to overwrite user work.

Disabling an extension changes behavior and can affect access to its data. Identify extension-owned fields and records first. Never test disabling on the only work. Preserve a backup, base-only version and an independent extended copy; test reenabling too.

Cover normal behavior, failures, repeats, old-data compatibility and restore. Reproduce a transfer defect, add a discriminating test and fix a copy before rerunning baseline cases. Preserve failed history; later success never rewrites an old receipt. Distinguish untested environments, permissions and performance from proven outcomes while preserving release-gate strictness. Each conclusion binds the actual source and observed case set.

Add a simple workflow rule, such as priority validation, with positive/negative cases. Compare baseline behavior, disable on a copy and verify return. Declare original contributions and the base used: executing a package proves neither authorship nor distribution rights over others’code.

A candidate contains requirements, sourceSHA, hashes, original data, protocols and rollback. Exclude platform binaries and proprietary configurations. Defense explains contribution and evidence limits:localPASSproves neither authorship nor certification. Publication, merge and production deployment require a separate owner decision. Material readiness and official release remain distinct states even when every automated check is green.
